\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بیخوابی} (bikhâbi)}{بیخوابی (bikhâbi)}]{\fa{بیخوابی} (bikhâbi) — insomnia, sleeplessness}

\label{lesson:FA-C499-bikhabi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a vitamin, then the Persian for being overweight.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بیخوابی}}
\textbf{\fa{بیخوابی}} (\emph{bikhâbi}) — \textquotedblleft{}insomnia, sleeplessness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{از} \fa{بیخوابی} \fa{رنج} \fa{میبرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u az bikhâbi ranj mibarad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She suffers from insomnia.
\end{quote}

\emph{bi-} 'without' + \emph{khâb} 'sleep' + \emph{-i}. \emph{az chizi ranj bordan} — to suffer from something.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bikhâbi} is built on native Persian parts: \emph{bi-}, 'without', \emph{khâb}, 'sleep', which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian and on to PIE \emph{swep-}, 'to sleep' (EtymDB), and the ending \emph{-i}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bikhâbi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bikhâbi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bikhâbi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a vitamin, then the Persian for being overweight, then say \emph{bikhâbi} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خروپف} \fa{کردن} (khoropof kardan)}{خروپف کردن (khoropof kardan)}]{\fa{خروپف} \fa{کردن} (khoropof kardan) — to snore}

\label{lesson:FA-C499-khoropof-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for being overweight, then the Persian for insomnia.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خروپف} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{خروپف} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{khoropof kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to snore\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدربزرگ} \fa{شبها} \fa{بلند} \fa{خروپف} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pedarbozorg shabhâ boland khoropof mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandfather snores loudly at night.
\end{quote}

\emph{khoropof} copies the sound: \emph{khor} breathing in, \emph{pof} breathing out. + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khoropof} is usually explained as an imitative word built on the sound of snoring, \emph{khor} and \emph{pof} joined by \emph{o}, 'and'. \emph{kardan}, 'to do', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for being overweight, then the Persian for insomnia, then say \emph{khoropof kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کابوس} (kâbus)}{کابوس (kâbus)}]{\fa{کابوس} (kâbus) — a nightmare}

\label{lesson:FA-C499-kabus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for insomnia, then the Persian for to snore.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کابوس}}
\textbf{\fa{کابوس}} (\emph{kâbus}) — \textquotedblleft{}a nightmare\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دیشب} \fa{کابوس} \fa{دیدم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dishab kâbus didam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I had a nightmare last night.
\end{quote}

\emph{kâbus didan} — to have a nightmare, like \emph{khâb didan} 'to dream'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kâbus} comes from Arabic \emph{kābūs}, 'nightmare' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خوابالود} (khâbâlud)}{خوابالود (khâbâlud)}]{\fa{خوابالود} (khâbâlud) — sleepy, drowsy}

\label{lesson:FA-C499-khabalud}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to snore, then the Persian for a nightmare.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خوابالود}}
\textbf{\fa{خوابالود}} (\emph{khâbâlud}) — \textquotedblleft{}sleepy, drowsy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{صبحها} \fa{خوابالود} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u sobhhâ khâbâlud ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He's sleepy in the mornings.
\end{quote}

\emph{khâb} 'sleep' + \emph{-âlud} 'smeared with', the same piece as in \emph{âlude} 'polluted'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khâbâlud} is built on native Persian \emph{khâb}, 'sleep', which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian (EtymDB), and \emph{-âlud}, 'smeared with', the piece behind \emph{âlude}, 'polluted'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خواب} \fa{ماندن} (khâb mândan)}{خواب ماندن (khâb mândan)}]{\fa{خواب} \fa{ماندن} (khâb mândan) — to oversleep}

\label{lesson:FA-C499-khab-mandan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a nightmare, then the Persian for sleepy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خواب} \fa{ماندن}}
\textbf{\fa{خواب} \fa{ماندن}} (\emph{khâb mândan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to oversleep\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{امروز} \fa{خواب} \fa{ماندم} \fa{و} \fa{دیر} \fa{به} \fa{کلاس} \fa{رسیدم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{emruz khâb mândam va dir be kelâs residam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Today I overslept and got to class late.
\end{quote}

\emph{khâb} 'sleep' + \emph{mândan} 'to stay'; present stem \emph{mân-}: to stay asleep.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khâb mândan} is built on two inherited words: \emph{khâb}, 'sleep', and \emph{mândan}, 'to stay', both of which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
